AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Motor Cortex Stimulation (MCS) was introduced in the early 1990's by Tsubokawa and his group for patients diagnosed with drug-resistant, central neuropathic pain. Inconsistencies concerning the details of this therapy and its outcomes and poor methodology of most clinical essays, divide the neuromodulation society worldwide in "believers" and "non-believers". A European expert meeting was organized in Brussels, Belgium by the Benelux Neuromodulation Society (BNS)in order to develop uniform MCS protocols in the pre-, intra- and post-operative course.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: An expert meeting was organized and a questionnaire was sent out to all the invited participants prior to this expert meeting. An extensive literature research was conducted in order to enrich the results.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Topics that were addressed during the expert meeting were: 1) inclusion and exclusion criteria, 2) targeting and methods of stimulation, 3) effects of MCS, and 4) results from the questionnaire.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Substantial commonalities, but also important methodological divergencies emerged from the discussion of MCS experts from seven European Centers. From this meeting and questionnaire, all participants concluded that there is a need for more homogenous standardized protocols for MCS regarding patient selection, implantation procedure, stimulation parameters and follow-up-course.
